clue.text: A rotten rotter?

parts.note: an egg that has gone off is literally rotten, and a rotter is a scoundrel, so the phrase for a no-good person also describes a spoiled egg

explanation.surface: A thoroughly worthless scoundrel, described twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a worthless, untrustworthy person, a figurative spoiled egg.

clue.text: Chest requiring reparative surgery?

definitions.meaning: the bosom or upper torso, also a sculpted head and shoulders
slang for broken, in need of repair

explanation.surface: A chest that needs an operation to put it right.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a woman's chest and, informally, something broken.

clue.text: Jerk brings pariah's name up with low voice

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the idiom 'his name is mud' is said of a disgraced person
bass is the lowest male singing voice

explanation.surface: A fool spreads an outcast's name about in a deep voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MUD into DUM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerk and this vulgar American word are both insults for a stupid person.

clue.text: See 19
Cricket sides seen occasionally

definitions.meaning: in cricket the off side and the on side are the two halves of the field either side of the batter

explanation.surface: Fielding positions at a cricket match are only sometimes visible.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side; 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for intermittently, happening from time to time.

clue.text: Sensation of ants crawling on skin I see in an arranged pattern

definitions.text: Sensation of ants crawling on skin

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a formation is an arranged pattern
C sounds like see, a common crossword convention

explanation.surface: A creepy feeling of insects on the skin, with a pattern to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term, from Latin formica for ant, names a tingling feeling like insects on the skin.

clue.text: Athletic female runner

definitions.meaning: a strong, sporty woman, after the warrior women of Greek legend
a river is a runner in crossword terms; this one flows through South America

explanation.surface: A sporty woman who runs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of the legendary warrior women and of the great South American river.

clue.text: Pressing unnecessary key, grave message sarcastic

parts.note: D is a musical key
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones
dry humour is wry or sarcastic

explanation.surface: Hitting a superfluous key on the keyboard produces a grimly sarcastic note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' means ironing, not pushing a key: the definition describes clothes that need no iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes labelled this way are hung wet and dry without creases, so ironing is not needed.

clue.text: Take lid off global power to fill void, at last going digital

indicators.note: one piece fills the other, sitting inside it
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: null means void or empty

indicators.note: in a down clue the lid is the top, the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: America is the world superpower

explanation.surface: A political takeover of a superpower filling a vacuum ends with going digital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take lid off' leaves MERICA; 'at last going' cuts NULL to NUL, which MERICA fills.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital and this word both describe things expressed in numbers.

clue.text: Polynesian islands populated by small Indian grub

indicators.note: islands populated by something have it inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Samoa is an island group in Polynesia
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A Pacific island group full of tiny Indian snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This fried pastry is a classic Indian snack, and grub is slang for food.

clue.text: Something living in whom sin a grotesque recollection

indicators.note: read as re-collection, collecting again in the opposite direction, so the letters are picked up backwards
the answer sits in the run of letters across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A person whose wrongdoing comes back to them as a horrible memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'whoM SIN A GROtesque', and 'recollection' says read those letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, plant or animal, is called by this biological term.

clue.text: What may suggest I get an illness

parts.words: What may suggest I get an
parts.note: the answer read as a cryptic instruction: the word before it is fodder and the word after it an anagram signal, which jumbles those letters into the three clue words

explanation.surface: A question about symptoms that make someone think they are falling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: rearranging the first word of the answer, with the second word as the anagram signal, gives I GET AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anorexia and bulimia are examples of this kind of serious condition, an illness of the mind and body.

clue.text: Barking dog with green man, funny little chap outside

indicators.note: barking means mad in British slang, so the letters go crazy

explanation.surface: A dog barks at a green figure, a comic little fellow standing outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A small comic figurine standing in a flowerbed outdoors is exactly this ornament.

clue.text: Day ran short during strike for final action

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, so it happens during it

parts.note: to lash is to strike, as with a whip
Thur is the short form of Thursday

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A day's stoppage was cut short during industrial action, the workers' last move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims RAN to RA; THUR plus RA go 'during' LASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A last showy effort or farewell performance before retirement is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Bastard lived locally, friendless, broken, imprisoning husband

indicators.note: the outer letters enclose the single letter like a prisoner
broken means smashed into a new order
read as friend-less: the letters for a friend, ally, are taken away

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in family trees

explanation.surface: An illegitimate child who lived nearby, alone and broken, keeps a husband locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendless' reads as friend-less, so the letters for a friend (ALLY) go; 'broken' rearranges what is left into LOVECILD, and 'imprisoning' puts the H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for a child born to unmarried parents, an illegitimate child.

clue.text: Harmony, say, in act evens out

indicators.note: taking out the even-numbered letters leaves only the odd ones

explanation.surface: A theatre group achieving harmony by smoothing out their act.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove letters 2, 4, 6 and 8 of 'say in act' and the odd letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in step or in harmony with something is a synonym of this short form of synchronisation.

clue.text: Relax with honourable Ivy League leaders in power

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: clout means influence or power

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Unwinding with prestigious university heads who hold power.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrasal verb is slang for unwinding or calming down.

clue.text: Weakness that grips strongly?

definitions.meaning: a moral failing or bad habit
a workshop tool with jaws that clamp a piece of work tight, spelt the same way in British English

explanation.surface: A failing that won't let go of you.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral failing is one sense; the bench clamp (spelt vise in America) is the other.

clue.text: Happy matter

definitions.meaning: satisfied, pleased (stressed on the second syllable)
the substance of something, what it contains (stressed on the first syllable)

explanation.surface: Pleased about something.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling means satisfied or pleased, and also the substance of a text.

clue.text: Sweet shop guarantees hot toffee fudge, unsurprisingly lovely, for starters

parts.note: a deli, delicatessen, is a kind of shop

indicators.note: the starters of words are their opening letters

parts.words: guarantees hot toffee fudge, unsurprisingly lovely

explanation.surface: A confectioner promises its toffee and fudge will taste lovely, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like the start of 'sweet shop' but is the definition; the shop is just DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and charming are synonyms for delightful, pleasing in nature.

clue.text: Hollywood's behind God-awful ghastly big old film

parts.note: in American English fanny means the buttocks

indicators.note: terrible, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Tinseltown's backside, ghastly in a terrible big old movie.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the word is ruder, hence 'Hollywood's'; 'God-awful' shuffles GHASTLY BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1944 British costume melodrama from Gainsborough Pictures is an old film.

clue.text: Cashier, snitch?

definitions.meaning: a bank clerk who handles cash

explanation.surface: A bank cashier who informs on others.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank clerk has this title, and so does one who tells tales.

clue.text: Tory minister back on the drink reaches valleys, through which views magnified?

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories

indicators.note: the word is turned backwards

parts.note: Rev, the Reverend, is a title for a minister
gin is a drink
glens are Scottish valleys

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician, back on the bottle, heads to the Welsh valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REV to VER. 'on' and 'reaches' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A convex lens bends light rays to meet, magnifying what is seen through it.

clue.text: Taste relegation

definitions.meaning: a small amount of drink, a sip
a fall to a lower division in sport

explanation.surface: A taste of demotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny sip of drink is one sense; a fall to a lower league is the other.

clue.text: Promise to wrap box, to say the least!

indicators.note: the outer piece wraps around the inner one

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay
the box is British slang for television, the telly

explanation.surface: Someone promises to gift-wrap a parcel, and says so emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic exclamations used to stress how understated a remark is.

clue.text: Endless bend or yew, crafted by him?

definitions.text: Endless bend or yew, crafted by him?

indicators.note: crafted means fashioned, so the letters are shaped into a new order
read as end-less: the letters spelling end are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman who bends yew wood into a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips END from 'bend', leaving B; that plus OR YEW is rearranged. The whole clue also describes the craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional craftsman who makes archery bows, often of yew, has this trade name.

clue.text: Put off, as Heath's volte-face went wrong

indicators.note: an about-turn, so the name is turned round

parts.note: Ted Heath was a British Conservative prime minister of the 1970s
erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A prime minister's U-turn was a mistake, as it turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was UK prime minister 1970–74; 'volte-face' turns his name round, giving DET.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discouraged from acting is to be put off or dissuaded.

clue.text: Don't go down river during drink

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

explanation.surface: Advice to stay afloat while drinking on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Not going to bed, remaining awake late, is the idiomatic sense here.
